correctness.rationale: PASS: For a binary linear word, each greedy complete two-letter arch corresponds to one disjoint unequal-adjacency edge and conversely, so universality index equals path matching number. In the cyclic transition subgraph, deleting each cut edge changes matching number by one only at odd-indexed edges of odd-length 1-runs. The fully alternating even case has no loss. Even 1-runs give a unique cyclic monomer/dimer tiling except the all-ones transition string with two tilings; the 2-to-1 lift from even-parity transition strings to indexed words and trace of [[1,1],[u,0]] give R_(n,k)=2n/(n-k)*binom(n-k,k)-2*[n=2k,k>=1], and R_n=2*(L_n-[n even]). n=1 and 2 boundaries were checked. Independently constructed exhaustive subsequence tests over all binary words n<=12 check every cyclic cut, bad-cut positions, and refined counts. These finite checks corroborate, not replace, the unrestricted matching/transfer proof.
